Title: Biomimetic kangaroo leg structure and Fe3O4/PDMS composite enable high-performance flexible capacitive pressure sensor with decoupled magnetic and pressure signals
Abstract: Magnetic flexible capacitive pressure sensors have garnered significant research interest due to their potential applications in intelligent sensing. However, two major technical bottlenecks currently exist: weak interfacial bonding between the biomimetic microstructure and the magnetic material, and difficulty in accurately distinguishing cross-interference between magnetic stimulation and pressure signals. To address these issues, this study proposes an integrated solution. A kangaroo-inspired dielectric layer is fabricated using 3D printing technology, with precise control of printing parameters to enhance structural integrity. A gradient dispersion process optimizes the uniformity of Fe3O4 particle distribution in polydimethylsiloxane, while finite element simulations determine the optimal particle ratio and structural parameters. Interfacial bonding technology reduces interfacial stress concentration and increases interfacial bonding strength; and the effective distinction between magnetic stimulation and pressure signals is achieved based on the positive and negative differences in capacitance signals. Experimental results demonstrate excellent sensor performance, including a high sensitivity of 1.331 kPa⁻¹ , a wide range up to 380 kPa, and a response time of only 40 ms. The sensor shows practical value in scenarios such as Morse code information transmission and encrypted communication systems, providing a new technological path for wearable electronic devices and information security. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Solar-powered multi-contaminant detection for real-time water quality monitoring
Abstract: Solar-powered Internet of Things (IoT) water-quality monitoring systems support real-time surveillance in off-grid environments, but evidence across sensing, power management, communication, and analytics remains fragmented. This review analysed 90 studies published between 2012 and 2025 that integrated sensing technologies, IoT architectures, and machine learning (ML) approaches. Over 80% of systems monitor physicochemical parameters such as pH, turbidity, temperature, electrical conductivity, and dissolved oxygen, while chemical contaminant detection appears in about 14% of studies and microbial monitoring in less than 10%. Typical photovoltaic capacities range from 10–50 W with 2–20 Ah batteries, yet fewer than 15% implement energy-aware sampling. LoRa/LoRaWAN dominates communication, and only 18% of systems use ML analytics. Limitations include fragmented sensing platforms, limited energy-adaptive design, and short deployments. A solar-centric co-design framework is proposed for scalable autonomous monitoring. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Reconfigurable free-space mode generation and detection enabled by an active photonic integrated circuit coupled to a passive mode-selective interface
Abstract: Optical mode-sorting and generation are used for a wide range of quantum, sensing and communication applications. High-speed switching between mode sets would allow photonics systems to react to changes in propagation channel in real time. Photonic-Integrated-Circuits (PICs) with phased arrays can rapidly reconfigure their function at MHz depending on installed modulators. As a reconfigurable photonic system, PIC can reconfigure significantly fast than spatial light modulators that are limited to less than 1 kHz. However, phased-arrays are bound by two-dimensional Nyquist-sampling limit and spacing between array elements leads to grating lobe formation, where many additional array elements are needed to mitigate these effects. We leverage a passive Multiple-Plane-Light-Converters (MPLC) as an Optical Mode-Selective Interface (OMSI), coupling a basis set of free-space Hermite Gaussian (HG) modes directly into an active optical mesh implemented on a PIC. The active mesh can generate or sort any free-space mode-set that can be created by a linear superposition of 15 HG modes. Without changing the physical system, we demonstrate the generation and sorting of four orthogonal mode groups, each with 15 modes, achieving a mean intermodal crosstalk for sorting of -22 dB. This approach can allow for rapidly reconfigurable mode-sorters that could be used for quantum or classical communications or sensing applications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Light confinement and frequency combs in nonlinear photonics
Abstract: The advent of high-quality optical microresonators and integrated photonic technologies has established Kerr frequency combs as a versatile platform for both fundamental studies and practical applications in modern photonics. These combs arise from the interplay between optical nonlinearity, dispersion, coherent driving, and cavity dissipation, leading to the emergence of a rich variety of self-organized structures and nonlinear dynamical states. This review presents a comprehensive overview of dissipative solitons and frequency-comb generation in passive Kerr resonators within the framework of the Lugiato–Lefever equation and its various extensions. We show how the Lugiato–Lefever model provides a unified theoretical description of nonlinear phenomena ranging from modulation instability, Turing patterns, and front propagation to dissipative Kerr solitons, multi-soliton states, and optical frequency-comb formation. Particular attention is devoted to the fundamental mechanisms governing light confinement, nonlinear wave localization, and soliton stabilization in driven-dissipative optical cavities. We further examine the influence of additional physical effects that enrich the dynamics of Kerr resonators, including polarization coupling and vector dissipative solitons, Raman scattering and Raman–Kerr comb generation, spectral filtering, spatially inhomogeneous pumping, and delayed optical feedback.Beyond stationary dissipative Kerr solitons, commonly known as dissipative Kerr solitons, passive optical resonators support a wide spectrum of dynamical behaviors, including breathing and drifting solitons, oscillatory localized states, front-mediated dynamics, and fully developed spatiotemporal chaos. Particular attention is devoted to the characterization of these complex regimes through the tools of nonlinear dynamics and dynamical systems theory. In this context, Lyapunov spectra and the Kaplan–Yorke dimension provide powerful indicators for identifying chaotic attractors, quantifying the dimensionality of the dynamics, and distinguishing spatiotemporal chaos from other forms of irregular behavior. Their application reveals the coexistence of chaotic states with dissipative Kerr solitons and homogeneous steady solutions, emphasizing the intricate organization of the phase space of driven-dissipative optical systems. These findings illustrate the deep connections between pattern formation, self-organization, front propagation, symmetry breaking, and high-dimensional nonlinear dynamics in Kerr resonators. This review offers a unified framework for understanding the physical mechanisms governing Kerr frequency-comb generation and control. The rapid progress achieved in material platforms, microresonator design, and photonic integration continues to expand the accessible dynamical regimes and performance of frequency-comb sources. As a result, Kerr comb technologies are becoming increasingly important for a broad range of applications, including precision metrology, spectroscopy, coherent optical communications, microwave photonics, sensing, and emerging quantum information and quantum sensing technologies. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Systematic study of spectral properties of bismuth-doped phosphosilicate fiber and broadband tunable lasing in O-band
Abstract: The spectral performance of a homemade bismuth phosphosilicate fiber (BPSF) has been systematically investigated, with a focus on thermal treatment optimization, double-pass amplification characteristics, and acousto-optic tunable filter (AOTF)-based laser tuning. The optimal thermal treatment temperature for BAC-P is determined to be approximately 400 °C, yielding a 1.1-times enhancement in gain performance compared to the pristine fiber. Under a double-pass configuration, the amplifier achieves a high gain exceeding 25 dB. Benefiting from the broadband gain, the AOTF-based laser tuning system demonstrates fast (∼ 17500 nm/s), linear, and precise wavelength tuning across the 1300–1400 nm range. A rapid wavelength switching time of ∼ 400 μs further confirms the reconfigurability of the AOTF system. These results not only provide new insights into the nature of BAC-P but also offer practical pathways for the deployment of bismuth-doped fibers in a wide range of applications, including dynamic optical communication systems, reconfigurable WDM optical networks, integrated broadband photonic devices, and biomedical sensing. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Title: Real-time integrated sea surface height and wave monitoring using a GNSS buoy based on PPP-B2b service
Abstract: High-precision real-time observation of sea surface height and wave parameters is essential for maritime safety, offshore engineering, disaster warning, and marine resource development. To overcome the high cost and operational complexity of in situ instruments and the limited spatiotemporal resolution of satellite remote sensing, this study proposes a global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) buoy method for integrated sea surface height and wave monitoring using the Beidou global navigation satellite system-3 (BDS-3) B2b service. Orbit, clock, and code bias corrections were used to build a dual-frequency ionosphere-free precise point positioning (PPP) model for precise buoy displacement estimation. Instantaneous sea surface elevation was derived from PPP-estimated buoy height after correcting for antenna geometry, buoy draft depth, and platform tilt, while wave parameters were retrieved using zero-crossing and spectral methods. Experiments included correction analysis, static and dynamic positioning tests, simulated wave tests, and a 24 h marine trial. In the marine experiment, the sea surface height root mean square error (RMSE) was 5.80 cm; significant wave height RMSEs were 3.72 and 4.33 cm; and average wave period RMSEs were 0.0916 and 0.0921 s for the zero-crossing and spectral methods, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrated, real-time, and accurate sea surface height and wave monitoring with a PPP-B2b-based GNSS buoy. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhu J.; Wang P.; Dai Q.; Fan L.
Title: A review of multiband photodetectors: From ultraviolet to infrared
Abstract: Photodetectors serve as core optoelectronic devices that convert optical signals into electrical signals, and they play an indispensable role in extensive fields such as optical communication, high-resolution imaging, precision sensing, national defense, and environmental monitoring. Although numerous existing review articles focus on limited spectral ranges or individual material systems, few efforts systematically summarize and compare the common challenges and cross-spectrum development opportunities of full-spectrum photodetectors covering ultraviolet, visible and infrared regions from a unified perspective. Centered on the core concept of multiband coordinated development, this review comprehensively summarizes the representative materials, device architectures, key performance indicators and diverse application scenarios for each spectral band, involving wide-bandgap semiconductors, perovskites, and two-dimensional materials. Beyond such comprehensive summary, this work further conducts an in-depth analysis of the universal cross-spectrum challenges restricting the advancement of photodetectors, including the standardization of performance evaluation systems, the compatibility of silicon-based integration technologies, the technical bottlenecks of large-area manufacturing, and overall economic accessibility. To address these critical issues, prospective strategies are proposed, including defect regulation engineering, heterogeneous structure integration, and integrated sensing and computing technologies. This review intends to provide a unique, challenge-driven and opportunity-oriented authoritative reference for the rational design, scalable fabrication and technological innovation of high-performance broad-spectrum photodetectors. It also delivers innovative insights to resolve the core obstacles that hinder the translational progress of photodetectors from laboratory research to practical commercial deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Evolution of narrow laser linewidth measurement techniques: short-delay and long-delay methods based on beat-frequency signals
Abstract: Laser linewidth is a core parameter characterizing laser coherence and frequency stability, which is critical for coherent optical communications, distributed fiber sensing, LiDAR, and quantum precision measurement. The conventional long-delay self-heterodyne method is mature but limited by bulky systems, high cost, and vulnerability to low-frequency 1/f noise. To address these drawbacks, short-delay techniques with delay lengths shorter than the laser coherence length have been rapidly developed, forming a new algorithm-driven measurement paradigm. This paper systematically reviews the evolution of narrow-linewidth laser measurement techniques, focusing on the comparison between classical long-delay self-heterodyne methods and emerging short-delay methods, including coherent envelope extraction, iterative demodulation, and advanced signal processing techniques. A delay-based self-heterodyne system is built for experimental verification. The illustrative experiments indicate the existence of an optimal delay range for short-delay schemes, and iterative demodulation shows superior noise suppression and stability over direct extremum extraction. This work establishes a unified framework linking intrinsic/Lorentzian/integrated linewidths to measurement paradigms, experimentally investigates the dependence of linewidth measurement performance on delay length, and quantitatively demonstrates that iterative demodulation exhibits greater robustness than the ADCCE method when the envelope is indistinct. The development trend from hardware-dependent long-delay architectures to algorithm-enhanced short-delay systems is highlighted, and future research directions are prospected. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Integrated photonic polarization synthesizer and analyzer
Abstract: Polarization-resolved control and measurement of optical fields are essential for a wide range of photonic systems, including coherent communication, polarimetric sensing, and quantum information processing. We present a photonic integrated circuit architecture that enables the generation and analysis of arbitrary polarization states. The device provides reconfigurable access to the full polarization degree of freedom of coherent light within a single integrated platform. We experimentally demonstrate arbitrary polarization state generation spanning the Poincaré sphere, as well as Stokes vector measurement on a chip. Unlike conventional Stokes measurements that rely on direct detection, the polarization state in this architecture is inferred from the phase settings required to interferometrically combine polarization-demultiplexed optical fields. As a result, the optical signal itself does not need to be detected or absorbed and remains available for subsequent optical-domain processing. The devices are fabricated in a commercial foundry using CMOS-compatible processes, enabling scalable and reproducible integration. By combining polarization generation and analysis in a compact and stable photonic circuit, this work eliminates the need for external polarization optics and provides a foundation for robust, polarization-enabled photonic integrated systems. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Dynamically reconfigurable multi-channel filters enabled by reflectivity-engineered Fabry–Pérot cavities
Abstract: Integrated photonic filters are key building blocks for classical optical communications, microwave photonics, and quantum photonics. Although multi-channel filters have been widely investigated, flexible control of the number of transmission channels remains limited by the absence of a unified theoretical framework and systematic experimental validation. In conventional structures such as microring resonators, reconfiguration typically affects all resonance channels simultaneously, making independent channel control difficult. Here, we propose an integrated Fabry–Pérot (FP) cavity filter that enables simultaneous tuning of both the number of transmission channels and their spectral positions. Inspired by traditional FP cavities used in passive sensing, we integrate the FP structure into an actively reconfigurable filter and engineer asymmetric mirror reflectivities to dynamically adjust the channel count. Waveguide Bragg gratings (WBGs) with excellent stopband characteristics serve as the cavity mirrors, with their reflectivities tuned via the thermo-optic effect. By setting both mirrors to high reflectivity or by setting one high and the other low, the resonance strength within the overlapping stopband can be flexibly controlled. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate dynamic switching among three-channel, two-channel, and single-channel states, with channel shifts of 10.34 nm, 10.77 nm, and 2.90 nm, respectively. The proposed architecture bridges a key gap in reconfigurable filter design and is fully compatible with standard fabrication processes, offering attractive scalability for large-scale photonic integration. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Unified Geometric-Phase metasurface for tunable Dual-Band Full-Polarization Terahertz wavefront control
Abstract: Precise and simultaneous control of orthogonal polarization states across discrete spectral windows remains a fundamental challenge in terahertz (THz) photonics. Here, we demonstrate a unified geometric phase platform for multifunctional and reconfigurable wavefront engineering based on a phase-change metasurface. By exploiting Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase modulation with anisotropic polarization coupling of the symmetry-engineered S-shaped meta-atom, the metasurface achieves dual-band high-efficiency polarization conversion ratio (PCR > 0.8) for both circular polarization (CP) and linear polarization (LP). Moreover, a phase superposition strategy enables focused OAM, achieving simultaneous point focusing and helical phase control within a single device. Title: An integrated monolithic photonic accelerometer with on-chip fringe-counting
Abstract: Photonic integrated circuits have transformed optical communication and information processing, yet their potential for precision inertial sensing remains largely untapped. To date, photonic accelerometers have been constrained by readout complexity, limited dynamic range, and insufficient experimental validation. Here we present the design, modelling, and experimental characterization of an integrated photonic accelerometer that combines high sensitivity with substantially enhanced dynamic range via phase-unwrapping. The device achieves a measured noise floor of 2.0µg/Hz, with a pathway towards ~10ng/Hz through simultaneous scaling of the input optical power and the number of waveguide loops on the cantilever — together projected to bring the input-referred shot-noise-limited sensitivity to the thermal-mechanical noise floor. By incorporating ellipse-fitting-based phase-unwrapping, the sensor enables accurate phase recovery over a substantially expanded measurement range, yielding a 39 dB improvement in dynamic range compared to a conventional Mach–Zehnder interferometer. To our knowledge, this is the first photonic integrated circuit accelerometer to incorporate fringe-counting functionality in a monolithic chip, and the first systematic study of such a strategy in integrated photonic inertial sensors. The photonic hardware enabling open-loop fringe counting — two Mach–Zehnder interferometers with a nominal quarter-wavelength inter-arm path-length offset, whose actual inter-interferometer phase difference is recovered from an in-situ ellipse fit — is monolithically integrated on the silicon-nitride chip, while the ellipse-fit phase-unwrapping algorithm runs in post-processing without active biasing or feedback control. These results establish integrated photonics as a promising platform for high-dynamic-range inertial sensing and a route to chip-scale accelerometers that could surpass existing chip-based technologies. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A multifunctional soft microrobot for untethered targeted delivery and temperature mapping
Abstract: Wireless intelligent microrobots offer a promising solution for precision medicine in deep physiological lumens. However, overcoming the limitation of single-functionality and achieving efficient coordination between autonomous microenvironment sensing and mechanical actuation within a single microsystem remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a wireless soft microrobot (T-SMR) based on intelligent nanocomposite materials that integrates magnetically controlled shape morphing with dynamic temperature-mapping capabilities. Owing to the deep integration of anisotropically magnetized particles and thermoresponsive microcapsules within the polymer network, the system can undergo a controllable conformational transformation from a two-dimensional planar configuration to a tightly coiled three-dimensional helical structure under magnetic actuation, enabling non-destructive cargo encapsulation and active transportation. Title: Dual-RIS enhanced ISAC with movable antennas: Dead zone sensing
Abstract: In a single reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) aided integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system utilizing a fixed position antenna (FPA) array to serve blocked targets, the performance is constrained by limited dead zone coverage and insufficient spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs). A movable antenna (MA)-enhanced dual-RIS-aided ISAC architecture is proposed in this paper to mitigate these issues. In this framework, the dual-RIS is utilized to establish cooperative virtual line-of-sight (LoS) links for extended range, while the system gain is further enhanced by exploiting the channel reshaping capability of MAs. A joint optimization problem is formulated to maximize the minimum beampattern gain at the dual-RIS via the joint design of the beam covariance matrix, phase shifts, and MA positions. An alternating optimization strategy employing alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), semidefinite relaxation (SDR) with Gaussian randomization, and successive convex approximation (SCA) is proposed to tackle this problem. Furthermore, discrete phase shifts for the dual-RIS are considered to accommodate practical hardware constraints. Numerical results demonstrate that the dual-RIS system outperforms the single-RIS benchmark by 126% in beampattern gain, through the additional beamforming gain and spatial diversity. Title: Spin-photon qubits for scalable quantum network

Special attention is given to silicon-based emitters, particularly G, T, C- and Ci-centers, which promise monolithic integration with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology and telecom-band operation. We classify these systems based on spin-photon interface availability, CMOS process compatibility, and emitter scalability. We also discuss recent advances in cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED), including Purcell enhancement and quality factor engineering in integrated photonic (circuits) environments. The work highlights emerging demonstrations of quantum networking over metropolitan scales and outlines the trajectory toward chip-scale quantum photonic integrated circuits (QPICs). Title: OTFS channel estimation in highly dynamic wireless environments: Key technologies, applications, and future challenges
Abstract: As sixth-generation mobile communications (6G) evolve toward Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGIN) and high-mobility scenarios, the performance of traditional orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technology is limited by severe Doppler shifts. Orthogonal time-frequency-space (OTFS) modulation technology transforms time-varying channels into quasi-static channels through signal processing in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, making it a key technology for addressing the challenges of high-mobility communications. This paper provides a comprehensive review of OTFS technology. First, it explains the modulation principles of OTFS and its core characteristics in the DD domain. Second, it systematically classifies channel estimation methods, covering pilot-based, channel sparsity-based (compressed sensing/Bayesian learning), and deep learning-based methods. Subsequently, the paper explores the integrated design of OTFS with Integrated Sensing and Communication(ISAC), Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS), and MIMO technologies, as well as the current status of its applications in typical scenarios such as Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X), Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. Title: Gate-tunable mid-infrared electroluminescence from Te/MoS2 p-n heterojunctions
Abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) emitters are critical components in advanced photonic systems, driving progress in fields such as chemical sensing, environmental monitoring, medical diagnostics, thermal imaging and free-space communications. Recent MIR emitters based on two-dimensional (2D) materials such as black phosphorus (BP) is more suitable for on-chip applications but faces challenges related to stability and emission efficiency. Title: ISAC beamforming for low-altitude wireless scenarios: Iterative Riemannian optimization on the complex sphere manifold
Abstract: This paper studies unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) aiming to achieve both sensing and communication functions. The UAV, deployed as an aerial access point (AP), leverages strong line-of-sight (LoS) air-to-ground (A2G) links to communicate with user equipments (UEs) and detect non-cooperative targets. The core challenge in ISAC beamforming design stems from the highly nonconvex nature of key performance metrics, namely the communication sum‑rate (SR) and the sensing Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address the resulting bi-objective non-convex optimization problem, we propose a Riemannian optimization algorithm on the complex sphere manifold (IROCSM), which is designed to prioritize convergence speed on the premise of guaranteed communication/sensing performance. Since the original objective function is analytically smooth, its complex structure induces potentially non-smooth numerical behavior in the Riemannian gradient on the manifold, we construct smooth surrogate functions for the joint communication and sensing objectives to adapt to manifold optimization, while embedding the transmit power constraint into the complex sphere manifold to transform the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one. In contrast to conventional relaxation-based approaches, this manifold optimization framework retains the problem’s nonconvexity while exploiting the geometric advantages to avoid relaxation errors. Consequently, the approach accelerates convergence without incurring approximation errors. Furthermore, convergence analysis confirms that the algorithm converges to a local optimal and Pareto frontier analysis quantitatively characterizes the tradeoff between communication and sensing performance. Simulation results demonstrate that IROCSM converges far faster than other approaches, delivering comparable SR and CRLB performance while maintaining superior computational efficiency in large-scale antenna scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Sensing-driven CSI acquisition in backscatter-assisted mmWave ISAC networks
Abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) enables high-resolution sensing but suffers from severe link blockages. Then the CSI parameters are reconstructed by combining user location information. Title: An end-to-end IoT framework for road defect and air quality inspection via mobile sensing and camera-LiDAR fusion
Abstract: Regular inspection of environmental and road network conditions is indispensable for urban maintenance, directly impacting public safety and economic sustainability in cities and communities. However, current practices heavily rely on manual efforts by specialized inspectors and engineers, lacking an integrated urban scanning system that supports automated data collection, analysis, communication, and visualization while yielding timely decision-making. To address this gap, this paper proposes an end-to-end mobile scanning framework for the inspection of urban roads and environment based on Internet of Things (IoT), robotic sensing and edge intelligence. Unlike traditional approaches that treat data acquisition and analysis as separate stages, this framework performs multi-sensor fusion (location, image, and point cloud) directly at the edge. Specifically, a lightweight attention-enhanced YOLOv11 instance segmentation model is adapted for on-device inference and integrated with an efficient camera-LiDAR calibration strategy to enable the localization and quantification of road defects directly at the edge. To reconcile the trade-off between communication bandwidth and coverage in complex urban environments, a hybrid data transmission strategy is developed: raw high-dimensional data is buffered locally, while critical semantic indicators are transmitted via Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN). This ensures robust edge-to-cloud connectivity even in cellular blind spots. Finally, a customized web interface integrates these heterogeneous data streams to provide users with timely updated, interactive spatiotemporal visualization. The framework is validated through two scales of field experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in providing continuous assessments of road conditions updated every 2.02 s and environmental quality updated every 30 s, thereby advancing intelligent infrastructure management and urban informatics. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Chemometric and machine-learning strategies for calibration transfer and uncertainty quantification in portable optical analytical systems

A comprehensive protocol is developed, which integrates stepwise protocols for data acquisition, normalization against references, transfer-learning calibration, drift detection, and uncertainty propagation to perform independent quantitative analyses. Title: Broadband achromatic metalens for the short-wave infrared
Abstract: The 1.8-2.3 m band lies within the short-wavelength infrared (SWIR) region and serves as a key operational window for a wide range of applications, including quantum sensing, molecular spectroscopy, and free-space quantum and classical optical communication. Despite its significance, optical devices operating in this band still face two major challenges: chromatic aberration across the wide spectral range and the difficulty of integration due to bulky optical elements. Metalenses are composed of subwavelength nanostructures that locally control the phase and group delay of light, enabling precise wavefront shaping and broadband dispersion compensation. These capabilities make them highly promising for use in infrared optical systems, particularly in applications such as focusing and imaging for compact integrated devices. In this study, we propose a metalens design based on a CaF substrate, where each nanocell consists of a single-bar silicon structure. These nanocells are periodically arranged with a 900 nm period, enabling precise control of dispersion and phase. We further analyze the polarization distribution across the focal spot and find a weak wavelength dependence of the degree of polarization (DoP), which we attribute to the spatially varying polarization state in the high-NA focal region together with the wavelength-dependent anisotropic response of the nanostructures. Meanwhile, this design offers a compact, broadband, and high-performance approach for beam collimation and wavefront shaping in the SWIR band, showing promising potential for applications in quantum communication and sensing systems. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Hybrid real-synthetic dataset framework for robotic hazard detection in industrial environments
Abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial environments requires the development of real-time hazard detection and environmental monitoring using intelligent robotic systems. Deployed in a functioning industrial testbed, RoboFusion collected real-time telemetry over 180 days using four sensor suites: two fixed units and two additional units mounted on Near-Field Communication (NFC) guided AMRs, each equipped with 12 sensors sampling at one-minute intervals. This deployment yielded approximately one million multi-modal sensor records, including temperature, humidity, gas concentrations, air quality, and pressure. Data streams were processed onboard using ESP32 microcontrollers, and they were transmitted via Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) to an Internet of Things (IoT) cloud platform. This framework augments non-hazardous data using statistical augmentation techniques, and it simulates hazardous data through multi-phase curve fitting, spatial propagation modeling, and location-aware hazard scenarios. The resulting synthetic dataset improves coverage of rare and safety-critical scenarios while maintaining consistency with real-world dynamics. Evaluation across four machine learning models, namely Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), demonstrates significant cross-domain gains. As an example, hazard F1 scores improved from 0.47 to 0.85 for the RF model, and from 0.16 to 0.79 for the SVM model when models trained on synthetic data were tested against real hazard events. Title: A human-centered VR-IoT implementation framework for disaster preparedness and response: A Sendai-aligned pilot feasibility study

Title: Aloe leaf-inspired and machine learning-driven porous carbon/FeSiAl flake metamaterials for low-frequency ultra-wideband electromagnetic absorption

Title: Resonator-enhanced distributed Bragg reflector lasers
Abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers are pivotal components for advanced optical communications, precision metrology, and microwave photonics. Title: RIS-aided joint radar sensing and communications: Covert beamforming design

Abstract: This paper proposes a covert beamforming design scheme with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) to enhance the transmission security of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems. To address this issue, we propose an alternating optimization framework, which decomposes the original problem into two subproblems: active beamforming and passive beamforming. These subproblems are efficiently solved by using techniques such as successive convex approximation (SCA) and convex preserving transformation. Title: Mid-infrared low-loss Huygens’ meta-waveguide based on the resonant Kerker effect

Title: An integrated, simulation-based framework linking satellite fire patterns and wireless sensor network planning in Tunisia
Abstract: Wildfire risk assessment and monitoring remain critical challenges in Mediterranean ecosystems, particularly in North Africa, where recurrent ignition patterns threaten forested landscapes and rural livelihoods. This study presents an integrated, simulation-based framework that links retrospective satellite fire observations with spatial wildfire risk estimation and wireless sensor network (WSN) deployment analysis in Tunisia. Historical NASA FIRMS VIIRS fire detections (2022–2025) are analyzed using multiple spatial clustering algorithms to identify persistent ignition corridors. Supervised learning models, evaluated under spatial cross-validation and strict temporal splits, are employed to generate static wildfire occurrence likelihood surfaces. A ConvLSTM model is examined as an exploratory component to assess short-term spatiotemporal patterns in fire activity. Wildfire risk information is subsequently incorporated into a simulation-based, multi-objective WSN deployment framework solved using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Simulation results obtained under idealized assumptions indicate that hotspot-informed WSN deployment strategies can reduce average inter-node distance by approximately 28% and communication energy consumption by approximately 35% relative to a uniform grid baseline. While the proposed framework does not constitute an operational early-warning system, it provides a reproducible methodology for translating satellite-derived wildfire risk information into monitoring infrastructure planning, with relevance for fire-prone regions in Tunisia and similar Mediterranean environments. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Polarimetric photodetector based on quasi-1D Ta2NiSe5/2D MoSe2 heterojunction with polarization inversion for multidimensional optical encoding and artificial vision
Source title: Journal of Materials Science and Technology
Abstract: Polarization-sensitive photodetectors capable of simultaneously resolving optical intensity and polarization state provide expanded information dimensions for remote polarization imaging, optical communication, and artificial vision. However, most existing systems rely on external polarization optics or exhibit weak coupling between spectral and polarization degrees of freedom, limiting their integration and information-processing capability. Here, we report a mixed-dimensional heterojunction by integrating quasi-1D Ta2NiSe5 with 2D MoSe2. Through interfacial band alignment and built-in electric field formation, the heterostructure device enables effective dark current suppression and dual-band polarization-spectral response capability. The Ta2NiSe5/MoSe2 photodetector exhibits broadband photodetection covering ultraviolet to near-infrared (200–1500 nm), with a high detectivity of 1.8 × 1010 Jones, a responsivity of 2340 mA /W, and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 717%, together with a fast temporal response of 48.5 μs. In addition, the device displays competitive polarization sensitivity with a polarization ratio value of 5.6 at 638 nm. More importantly, it delivers a strong polarization-sensitive response together with a pronounced wavelength-controlled polarization eigenstate switching behavior, where orthogonal polarization responses are realized between the visible (405 nm) and infrared (808 nm) regimes. Taking advantage of the multidimensional response characteristics, we demonstrated its polarization-spectral multiplexed imaging, multi-channel optical communication, and convolutional neural network-assisted image recognition, achieving an accuracy approaching 99%, highlighting the capability of the device for integrated sensing and computing. This work develops a functional heterostructure for multidimensional optoelectronics and provides a promising strategy toward next-generation intelligent vision systems, polarization communication technologies, and neuromorphic photonic devices. © 2026

Authors: Al Satai H.
Title: Underwater optical integrated sensing and communication as a networked architecture: A survey of communication, localization, alignment, and task-driven autonomy
Abstract: Underwater optical integrated sensing and communication is emerging at the intersection of high-rate underwater optical links, optical localization, beam alignment, docking guidance, and autonomous underwater vehicle networking. Existing studies often treat these functions separately, either as physical-layer communication links, localization algorithms, or robotics demonstrations. This survey argues that such a separation is insufficient because underwater optical links are governed by the same variables that sensing and control must estimate: range, orientation, pointing error, receiver field of view, blockage, water attenuation, scattering, turbulence, and platform mobility. The paper therefore reviews underwater optical sensing-communication integration as a networked architecture problem. It organizes work from January 2020 to April 2026 around five research questions covering the distinction between related and true integrated sensing and communication systems, the role of device/link/network/application layers, maturity of the literature, protocol mechanisms, and deployment readiness. The survey develops a four-layer architecture, separates adjacent enablers from true and networked integrated sensing and communication contributions, proposes a six-level maturity score, and compares representative systems in terms of communication performance, sensing observable, localization or guidance metric, validation method, water condition, mobility, topology, and network function. The review further analyzes candidate protocol mechanisms for directional medium access control, pose-aware routing, optical-acoustic handover, topology control, docking-station access, and multi-autonomous-underwater-vehicle coordination. The central finding is that the field has strong device-, link-, localization-, and docking-level evidence, but remains weak at the network layer. Future progress requires quantitative communication-sensing-network metrics, reproducible testbeds, switching criteria for optical-acoustic operation, failure recovery mechanisms, and experimentally validated architectures that connect optical observations to network decisions. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Indoor human visible light positioning using optical camera geometry and multilayer perceptron-based error compensation towards VLC-based integrated sensing and communication
Abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) has gradually evolved from conventional lighting-communication integration toward the convergence of lighting, communication, and sensing functionalities, commonly referred to as VLC-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). Indoor visible light positioning (VLP) has attracted significant attention; however, most existing VLP studies mainly focus on receiver (Rx) localization based on received signal strength (RSS) or optical signal measurements, while human ground-plane localization using pose keypoints remains relatively less explored. In this work, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an indoor human ground-plane VLP system by integrating You-Only-Look-Once-Pose (YOLO-Pose), optical camera geometry, and multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based error compensation. YOLO-Pose is employed to detect human body keypoints and light-emitting-diode (LED) positions from captured images, while camera calibration and geometric projection are used to map the ankle midpoint of the detected human skeleton onto the floor plane in world coordinates, thereby providing a baseline geometry-based localization result. An MLP-based compensation model is then introduced to predict correction offsets in the x- and y-directions. Proof-of-concept experimental results show that, for the test trajectory, the proposed scheme reduces the mean localization error from 10.64 cm to 0.98 cm and the root mean square error (RMSE) from 12.44 cm to 1.42 cm. In addition, a preliminary optical wireless data transmission experiment is demonstrated using the same LED infrastructure, where directly modulated LED signals are separated by different radio-frequency (RF) carrier frequencies. These results show the potential of the proposed localization-oriented framework as a step towards indoor VLC-based ISAC applications. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Cai Y.; Ma S.; Shang L.; Hao X.; Zhang J.; Wang J.; Liu X.; Xu B.
Title: Research progress on infrared photodetectors based on low-dimensional black phosphorus materials
Source title: Physica E: Low-Dimensional Systems and Nanostructures
Abstract: Infrared (IR) detection is critical for night vision, spectroscopic sensing, and optical communications. Traditional IR photodetectors suffer from inherent limitations: high fabrication costs, mandatory cryogenic cooling, and poor silicon process compatibility. Low-dimensional materials offer a promising alternative, featuring tunable bandgaps, high carrier mobility, and strong light–matter interactions. Black phosphorus (BP) stands out for its layer-dependent direct bandgap, high carrier mobility, and remarkable in-plane anisotropy. However, although dark current can be partially suppressed via low-bias or photovoltaic modes, intrinsic thermally generated carriers remain a core bottleneck for room-temperature mid-infrared BP photodetectors compared with mature bulk systems. Most existing reviews focus on two-dimensional (2D) exfoliated BP flakes and their basic optoelectronic performance. From a multi-dimensional low-dimensional structure perspective, this review systematically summarizes recent advances in BP-based IR photodetectors. First, it introduces BP photodetection fundamentals and emerging physical phenomena—polariton field enhancement, ultrafast carrier dynamics, and moiré exciton engineering—with a critical comparison to other mainstream IR materials. It then covers BP's crystal structure, intrinsic properties, and synthesis strategies for zero-dimensional (0D), one-dimensional (1D), and two-dimensional (2D) BP nanostructures. Addressing BP's critical environmental instability, it clarifies the underlying degradation mechanism and summarizes mainstream stabilization approaches. It further reviews device architectures from single-pixel detectors and integrated focal plane arrays to printable imagers, revealing core performance-governing mechanisms. Finally, it identifies key challenges and prospects for stable, high-performance BP IR photodetectors. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Single-atom nanozyme-based wireless microfluidic sensing platform for noninvasive hyperuricemia diagnosis
Abstract: Hyperuricemia is characterized by abnormally elevated serum uric acid (UA) levels. Persistent hyperuricemia not only triggers gout but also causes damage to the kidneys and cardiovascular system. Therefore, utilizing non-invasive diagnostic methods for early and continuous monitoring is crucial for preventing disease progression. Herein, we reported a portable wireless electrochemical sensing platform constructed from SA-Pt/rGO/MOF catalysts prepared via photochemical deposition of platinum single atoms (Pt SAs) on reduced graphene oxide/metal-organic framework (rGO/MOF) composites. The designed single-atom catalysts (SACs) exhibited exceptional electrocatalytic activity toward UA oxidation, and the fabricated sensing platform demonstrated a broad linear detection range (1-1000 μM) and relatively low detection limit (1.12 μM), with excellent selectivity and reproducibility. To enhance direct biofluid analysis, we designed a hydrophilic surface-modified microfluidic device for enhanced collection efficiency. Building upon this device, the integrated wireless microfluidic electrochemical platform enabled quantitative UA analysis and correlation studies in serum and saliva from 10 hyperuricemia patients and 10 healthy volunteers, demonstrating promising clinical utility. This work not only extended SACs applications to ultrasensitive biomarker detection but also provided a feasible strategy for developing next-generation non-invasive point-of-care testing (POCT) devices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Energy-efficient neuromorphic computing for ultra-low latency cognitive radio: a hardware-software co-design framework for 6 G spectrum intelligence
Abstract: Sixth-generation (6 G) wireless networks demand cognitive radio systems that simultaneously achieve sub-millisecond latency and sustainable energy consumption – requirements conventional artificial intelligence approaches cannot meet. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design framework integrating neuromorphic computing with cognitive radio to address both constraints through brain-inspired spiking neural networks (SNNs). We systematically analyze five neuromorphic platforms – Intel Loihi 2, IBM TrueNorth, SpiNNaker, SpiNNaker 2, and Intel Hala Point – using standardized benchmarks from the Intel Neuromorphic Deep Noise Suppression (N-DNS) Challenge, demonstrating sub-millisecond spectrum decisions (50-170 s end-to-end latency) with energy consumption reduced by 100-1000 (31 pJ per spike) compared to conventional GPU-based approaches (2.5−12.5 J per operation). Our framework provides three novel contributions: (1) a unified co-design methodology optimizing spike encoding, network topology, and hardware mapping jointly to achieve 3 efficiency gains over independent optimization; (2) quantitative design rules for encoding selection – rate coding for signal-to-noise ratios below -10 dB, temporal coding for latency requirements below 100 s, and population coding for reliability exceeding 99.9%; and (3) experimental validation achieving 97.6% classification accuracy on real-world spectrum data from industrial IoT deployments consuming only 31 mW average power. Through five detailed case studies spanning industrial automation (99.9% uptime over 6 months), vehicle-to-everything communications (98.7% collision avoidance), defense applications (95% reliability under 40 dB jamming), smart cities (100,000 sensors), and healthcare (15-year implant lifetime), we demonstrate neuromorphic cognitive radio’s practical viability. The framework addresses critical deployment barriers including device variability mitigation (±20% threshold compensation), cross-platform algorithm portability, and RF-to-spike conversion interfaces. These results establish neuromorphic computing as a foundational technology for energy-constrained, latency-critical 6 G wireless systems, with implications extending to radar processing, electronic warfare, and satellite communications. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Emerging smartphone-based real-time monitoring for food freshness and spoilage assessment in stimuli-responsive smart packaging
Abstract: Smart packaging responsive to stimuli, coupled with smartphone-based sensing, could revolutionize the timely assessment of food freshness and spoilage throughout the supply chain. This review attempts to bridge the gap between smart packaging technologies responsive to chemical and physical stimuli (pH, temperature abuse, spoilage volatiles, etc.) and their translation into quantifiable digital signals through smartphone interfaces. For freshness and spoilage monitoring, “Four primary smartphone-integrated sensing modes are considered, RGB camera imaging, NFC-enabled systems, smartphone-assisted spectral analysis, and BLE sensors, while thermal imaging is discussed separately as a complementary temperature-monitoring modality. In this regard, machine learning is emerging as a valuable tool for neutralizing hardware variation, reducing false positive/negative outputs, and developing predictive models of spoilage. Other emerging interfaces, including QR codes as data gateways and IoT-enabled data ecosystems, are also discussed, while smartphone thermography is evaluated separately as a temperature-monitoring modality. On the other hand, with validated global standards and interoperable communication protocols, smartphone-based packaging moves the paradigm for food quality and spoilage monitoring from after-the-fact testing to proactive, data-driven assessment. A stepwise roadmap is proposed for validating and deploying these technologies for food-quality monitoring, early warning of spoilage-associated risks, and potential food-waste reduction. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: Polymer-Based Flexible Wireless Sensors for Health Monitoring
Abstract: A system-level review of polymer-based flexible wireless sensors for epidermal, subcutaneous, and short-term implantable health monitoring is presented, elucidating the coupling among materials, interfaces, and wireless links. Title: A broadband lithium tantalate-on-silicon nitride heterogeneous modulator for optical and terahertz communications and radar sensing
Abstract: Photonic integrated circuits have driven advances in optical interconnects, wireless communications, seamless sensing. Electro-optic modulators, which bridge the electronic and optical domains, act as the cornerstone of these systems. To address the ultra-broadband demands of next-generation information systems while enabling heterogeneous integration with other functional components, here we present a high-performance thin-film lithium tantalate-on-silicon nitride heterogeneous Mach-Zehnder modulator fabricated via micro-transfer printing. The device shows an insertion loss of 1.0 dB, an electro-optic bandwidth exceeding 110 GHz, and a power drift of ~0.3 dB over 72 h at quadrature bias. We employ the modulator for three typical scenarios in the applications of optical communications, fully photonic terahertz wireless communications, and radar sensing. It achieves optical data transmission rates beyond 375 Gbps, a record rate of 148 Gbps for wireless communications in the D-Band, and a range resolution of 1.2 cm with measured errors below 2 mm in the W-Band. These results pave the way for scalable, high-performance, cross-domain photonic chips for next-generation information networks. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: GSCF: A joint scheduling framework for service gap minimization and resource optimization in UAV-assisted edge computing
Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-assisted Mobile Edge Computing (UAV-MEC) provides flexible communication and edge-computing support in infrastructure-scarce environments such as wide-area forest monitoring. In these environments, complex terrain and vegetation attenuation reduce the number of feasible air–ground links, while bursty sensing events generate many deadline-constrained tasks and increase both service-gap risk and scheduling scale. To address these coupled challenges, this paper proposes the Geometrized Scheduling and Clustering Framework (GSCF), which provides a structured approximate decomposition of the coupled scheduling problem. First, the Integrated Incremental Stream Clustering (IISC) algorithm aggregates spatially correlated and service-compatible current-slot raw tasks into traceable micro-clusters while preserving the data volume, CPU-cycle demand, earliest deadline, service type, and representative location required by subsequent decisions. Second, a location-dependent energy-aware generalized topology mechanism jointly accounts for projected residual energy, movement cost, regional migration penalty, and spatial proximity to construct candidate UAV regions and horizontal targets. Third, mode-specific feasible-edge screening builds a candidate graph; Minimum Cost Maximum Flow (MCMF) generates a complete candidate assignment, Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions allocate UAV CPU resources, and aggregate validation with deterministic repair establishes constraint consistency. Experiments show that GSCF achieves the lowest system weighted cost and deadline-miss rate among the six evaluated algorithms. Compared with Distance-only and Static-Grid, it delays the first UAV-unavailability event by 16.60–19.85 and 56.45–60.00 slots, respectively. At a task load of 100, IISC reduces the solver time from 18.626 s to 1.295 s compared with No-IISC. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: AI-enabled integrated sensing, communication, and illumination in VLC/LiFi networks for 6G: Recent advances and future perspectives
Abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) and light fidelity (LiFi) are emerging as promising optical wireless technologies for sixth-generation (6G) networks, offering high-capacity, spatially confined, and electromagnetic-interference-free wireless access by exploiting existing lighting infrastructure. Beyond conventional data transmission, the same optical infrastructure can simultaneously support illumination, indoor positioning, and environmental sensing, a convergence formally defined as lighting, sensing, and communication (LiSAC). This review presents an integrated perspective on AI-enabled LiSAC in VLC/LiFi networks for 6G. The fundamentals of VLC/LiFi, including the Lambertian channel model, intensity-modulated direct-detection constraints, and LiFi networking architecture, are first introduced. The evolution from communication-oriented VLC toward coordinated LiSAC, encompassing visible-light positioning achieving decimeter-to-centimeter accuracy and visible-light sensing demonstrating occupancy and gesture recognition above 90% accuracy, is then reviewed. The role of artificial intelligence across channel estimation, signal detection, adaptive dimming, localization, resource allocation, and handover is examined, with deep reinforcement learning demonstrating up to 48% data rate improvement and federated learning enabling privacy-preserving distributed optimization. Photonic and device-level enablers, including GaN micro-LEDs with bandwidths exceeding 800 MHz, perovskite quantum dot color converters with bandwidths 40 times greater than conventional phosphors, wavelength-shifting fiber-based detectors, and optical intelligent reflecting surfaces, are reviewed as the hardware foundation for 6G LiSAC systems. Finally, key challenges, including LOS blockage, multi-function trade-offs, dataset scarcity, hardware–algorithm mismatch, real-time implementation, privacy, and standardization, are discussed alongside a structured three-horizon research roadmap. The review highlights that future VLC/LiFi systems must move toward AI-native, photonic-integrated, privacy-aware, and experimentally validated architectures capable of supporting multifunctional 6G services. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Decision-consistent online control for move-then-serve UAV-enabled integrated sensing and communication
Abstract: Move-then-serve control in vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems enabled by an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) requires the UAV to choose its motion before communication and sensing resources are optimized at the realized post-motion location. This timing turns mobility selection into a recourse decision in which each reachable location should be scored by the executable value obtained after local resource re-optimization at that same location. We develop a decision-consistent exact-execution controller (DCEE) for a UAV-assisted road corridor with data backlog, age of information (AoI), tracking uncertainty, flight cost, resource cost, and road-context cost. Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty is used as a causal reduction tool, while the central object is the executable post-motion value field. DCEE combines a smooth regularized design stage with unregularized post-motion resource execution. The analysis gives a statewise executed-value gap, primitive-error robustness, conditional long-run penalty/backlog guarantees, an explicit statewise Slater-type sufficient condition, a finite-candidate union (FC-Union) benchmark, and adaptive-altitude and multi-UAV recourse interfaces. The evaluation includes finite-family gap diagnostics, runtime and scalability tests, queue and slack diagnostics, model-sensitivity studies, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) baselines, and an altitude diagnostic. Under FC-Union, finite-family gaps are nonnegative, and all candidate evaluations satisfy the reference-eligibility test after deterministic rescue. In the lightweight balanced runtime diagnostic, DCEE averages 81.85 ms per slot for mobility-controller computation. In a held-out comparison with a shared unregularized post-motion backend, validation-tuned DCEE achieves lower mean penalty than proximal policy optimization (PPO), soft actor–critic (SAC), and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) mobility policies and reduces average backlog by 66.2%–67.7%. In a compact altitude diagnostic, DCEE-3D reduces backlog from 239.356 to 209.267 at comparable penalty. © 2026

Title: Electrode multiplexing enables scalable continuous molecular monitoring in interstitial fluid
Abstract: Continuous molecular monitoring in interstitial fluid could transform the real-time decoding of human physiology, but current wearable bioelectronics remain fundamentally constrained by hardware scaling, where each additional analyte typically requires dedicated sensing electrodes and circuitry. Here, we introduce an electrode multiplexing architecture that enables continuous multiplexed monitoring without increasing the number of electrodes. Central to this strategy is a dynamically reconfigurable ion-selective electrode that alternates between potentiometric sensing and counter electrode operation. This allows a single electrode to support multiple electrochemical modalities. Integrated with a nanoengineered gold nanoparticle-MXene interface and a microneedle-based wearable platform, the system enables continuous monitoring of glucose, lactate, and potassium ions in interstitial fluid with high sensitivity and operational stability through a wireless multiplexed sensing architecture (sensitivities of the glucose, lactate, and K+ sensors were 6.16 nA/mM, −1.77 nA/mM, and 55.86 mV/decade, respectively). The multiplexed sensor maintains stable electrochemical performance after repeated role-switching cycles while preserving ion sensitivity. Wireless in vivo monitoring in rats captured dynamic metabolic fluctuations with strong agreement to blood-based measurements, while human serum analysis demonstrated high clinical consistency across all analytes. By decoupling sensing dimensionality from hardware complexity, this work establishes electrode multiplexing as a scalable design principle for next-generation wearable bioelectronics and continuous molecular monitoring. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become increasingly popular across a wide range of civilian domains, from precision agriculture and environmental monitoring to infrastructure inspection and emergency response, driven by rapid advances in flight autonomy, onboard sensing and miniaturized computing hardware. Yet, for UAVs to move beyond mission-specific deployments and become truly integrated into daily operations, their role must evolve: rather than functioning as flight-centric platforms that execute predefined flight plans, they need to operate as service-centric edge computing nodes capable of dynamically hosting, executing and managing application services onboard. This paper presents a service-centric UAV edge node architecture that integrates lightweight Kubernetes (K3s) container orchestration on an ARM-based companion computer within a cloud–fog–edge continuum. The system enables dynamic deployment of containerized applications during flight, through a user-facing web portal. Recognizing that UAV operations in rural, remote or disaster-affected environments frequently encounter degraded or absent broadband terrestrial coverage, the paper further proposes and experimentally validates Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) connectivity, both terrestrial and satellite, as an innovative alternative communication solution of last resort. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental implementation of NB-IoT on UAV edge platforms. The NB-IoT link operates as a bidirectional channel, supporting uplink delivery of AI inference results and telemetry as well as downlink reception of mission commands such as arming, takeoff, waypoint updates and mode changes. Two complementary paths are evaluated: (i) terrestrial NB-IoT, providing near real-time connectivity validated through laboratory and real outdoor UAV flight tests with 0% packet loss across 324 messages and 1–2 s end-to-end latency; and (ii) Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) NB-IoT via a real 5G LEO satellite testbed, demonstrating reliable store-and-forward data offloading under realistic orbital constraints. The results demonstrate that NB-IoT provides a viable, standards-based fallback connectivity layer for service-centric UAV edge systems operating beyond the reach of broadband networks. © 2026 The Authors

Title: State-of-the-art and future directions in autonomous navigation for UAVs in GNSS-denied environments: A comprehensive review of techniques, architectures, and applications
Abstract: The widespread deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in complex operational settings remains constrained by reliance on Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for accurate positioning and attitude stabilization. This manuscript provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art methods and architectural frameworks that enable robust autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied, degraded, or jammed environments, including indoor spaces, underground tunnels, and dense urban canyons. The review establishes a clear taxonomy that classifies navigation strategies into relative localization methods (e.g., odometry and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, SLAM) and global localization methods based on external references and prior maps. A comparative synthesis is presented across core sensing modalities, visual, LiDAR, and inertial, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and their integration within high-performance fusion pipelines such as Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) and LiDAR-inertial systems. The article further surveys advanced approaches, including Ultra-Wideband (UWB) localization, Terrain-Aided Navigation (TAN), radar-based navigation, and Deep Learning and Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and discusses their roles within integrated and cooperative navigation architectures. Key operational challenges are examined, with emphasis on Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints, environmental variability, failure detection and recovery, and the long-term drift that can arise in relative methods without absolute correction. Benchmark-oriented comparisons are also synthesized to clarify reported performance trends and practical trade-offs across representative navigation frameworks. The manuscript concludes by outlining research directions focused on efficient learning models, reliable multi-modal fusion, semantic-aware mapping, and certifiable resilience mechanisms to support safety-critical GNSS-denied missions such as infrastructure inspection, search and rescue, and environmental monitoring, with relevance to both research and industrial development. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Zhou F.; Wang Y.; Shan F.; Wu W.
Title: Enhancing routing in dynamic and dense networks through UWB swarm ranging for embodied intelligence
Abstract: Embodied intelligence has emerged as a key direction in Artificial Intelligence and is playing an increasingly significant role across various domains. Small embodied agents/robots, such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), operate in swarm mode based on embodied intelligence and provide greater sensing and processing capabilities compared to individual agents/robots. However, they also introduce new challenges: dynamic and dense networks formed by resource-constrained embodied intelligent agents demand real-time, low forwarding overhead networking protocol. We leverage our previously proposed Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Swarm Ranging Protocol, and (1) propose a UWB-based link quality estimation method that leverages real-time inter-agent ranging to enable faster and more accurate estimation of link states, thereby mitigating the impact of network dynamics. We then (2) formulate a novel Multi-Point Relays (MPR) selection problem that aims to effectively reduce forwarding overhead while ensuring the Quality of Service (QoS) provided by selected relay nodes. An approximation algorithm is proposed, and its approximation ratio is analyzed. We also (3) design an integrated message format that combines ranging and routing functionalities, which is implemented on resource-constrained agents with a 168 MHz MCU and 192 KB memory. Lastly, both simulations and real-world experiments show that, our protocol shortens the round-trip time by approximately 54.7% compared to classic AODV protocol, while improving the packet delivery rate by approximately 17.3% over OLSR protocol. We also open-source our implementation on GitHub, providing a reproducible platform for further research and development: https://github.com/SEU-NetSI/crazyflie-firmware.git. © 2026

Author full names: Roussos, Konstantinos (36722299000); Mardini, Mahmoud (57220071557); Salvi, Maria Cristina (59678135900)
Title: Byzantine fortifications and their natural settings in crete: A geo-spatial analysis
Abstract: Byzantine fortifications are increasingly understood from contemporary research not as isolated or static military structures but as elements integrated into their environmental, social, and historical settings. This study examines three Middle Byzantine fortifications in the Kissamos region of northwestern Crete: Polyrrhenia, Malathyros, and Rokka. The sites, which vary in type and scale, date to the late 10th to early 13th centuries AD. Their placement is assessed through a combination of archaeological methods, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing, and additionally complemented with historical sources. The analysis considers the fortifications’ relative placement to nearby arable land, grazing areas, coastal access, and possible land routes. GIS results show that Polyrrhenia commanded wide views over the coastal plain and maintained intervisibility with Malathyros and Rokka, allowing for communication and coordinated defense. Malathyros, offered more limited coastal views, yet provided oversight toward the Spatha promontory and strengthened inland connectivity. Rokka oversaw fertile catchments and had quick access to the coast, functioning as a smaller but multifunctional stronghold. Least-cost path modeling indicates that the three fortified sites were within two to three hours walking distance, supporting mobility and resource access. Land use and land cover mapping confirms that the fortifications were embedded in productive agricultural and pastoral zones. These results suggest that the fortifications formed an interconnected system of defense, resource management, and communication rather than serving only as separate defensive outposts. They reflect a deliberate dual strategic objective, in which security and economic sustainability were intertwined, with fortifications safeguarding both population and production. This perspective enhances our broader understanding of how Byzantine frontier strategies integrated military needs with local resources and may offer a comparative framework for analyzing fortified landscapes, both in other areas of the island and across Greece or the wider Byzantine Empire. © 2026

Title: Integration of electrochemical sensors in organ-on-a-chip microfluidic platforms: Advances and perspectives
Abstract: Electrochemical sensors integrated into organ-on-a-chip (OoC) — single-organ systems and more complex multi-organ (body-on-a-chip) — microfluidic platforms constitute a rapidly advancing interface between biosensing, microfluidics, and microphysiological systems (MPS), with major implications for biomedical research, drug discovery, toxicology, and personalized medicine. By transducing biochemical and biophysical events at the tissue–device interface into quantifiable electrical signals, these sensors enable real-time, label-free, and highly sensitive monitoring of metabolites, ions, barrier integrity, and cellular activity under physiologically relevant conditions. Within OoC and MPS platforms, electrochemical sensing can be implemented through different integration strategies, including on-chip configurations such as in-line and on-line sensing directly embedded within microfluidic channels, as well as off-chip approaches. The integration of miniaturized and multiplexed electrochemical sensors into MPS enables continuous and high-throughput functional monitoring of key physiological parameters, including metabolic activity variation, biomolecules gradients, barrier function, and responses to drugs and toxic compounds. Multi-OoC configurations benefit from electrochemical readouts to interrogate dynamic inter-organ communication and systemic responses, supporting more predictive human-relevant models. This is mostly relevant for new approach methodologies (NAMs), which aim to reduce animal experimentation while improving human relevance and predictive accuracy. Overall, electrochemical sensor–integrated OoC/MPS platforms represent powerful NAMs aligned with 3Rs (replacement, reduction, and refinement) principles, enabling high-throughput screening, improved physiological relevance, and enhanced predictive modeling for drug development and regulatory applications. In this review, we address recent advances in electrochemical sensor integration within OoC and MPS platforms, discussing fabrication strategies, sensing modalities, and system-level architectures, as well as current challenges and future perspectives. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Brain-body crosstalk in T2DM: An integrative framework from central sensing to peripheral feedback
Abstract: Brain-body crosstalk describes the dynamic and bidirectional interactions between the central nervous system and peripheral organs, whereby the brain regulates systemic physiology while peripheral signals reciprocally influence central function. The pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has expanded beyond peripheral insulin resistance to encompass dysregulated bidirectional communication between the central nervous system and peripheral organs. Despite growing recognition of brain-body crosstalk in T2DM, existing studies have largely examined individual pathways in isolation, limiting an integrated understanding of neuro-metabolic regulation. Here, we conceptualize brain–body crosstalk as a hierarchical yet reciprocal network comprising central sensing and integration, peripheral execution, and feedback regulation, and further frame its disruption in T2DM as a self-reinforcing cascade of dysregulation. We systematically examine how central neural circuits modulate peripheral organs via autonomic and neuroendocrine outputs, and how peripheral metabolic, immune, and microbial signals feedback to reshape central function. Building on this integrative framework, we critically assess emerging neuromodulation strategies and highlight key unresolved questions. This framework positions T2DM as a disorder of progressively destabilized brain–body homeostasis and identifies critical points at which this pathological feedback loop may be therapeutically interrupted. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Enabling OFDM-based radar for moving target detection: A waveform design for enhanced Doppler tolerance and superior range sidelobes
Abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) has been widely adopted in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems due to its flexible multi-carrier structure. However, strict subcarrier orthogonality makes OFDM highly sensitive to Doppler shifts, which leads to severe performance degradation in high mobility sensing scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes an OFDM radar waveform design that jointly enhances Doppler tolerance, suppresses range sidelobes, and controls the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). The resulting quartic fractional problem is formulated to shape the discrete ambiguity function (AF) toward a desired diagonal-ridge structure under unimodular and oversampled PAPR constraints. To solve this challenging problem, an efficient algorithm is developed by integrating Dinkelbach’s transform, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and the majorization-minimization (MM) method. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed design. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Bifunctional WO₃ NPs/p-Si heterojunction for integrated acetone gas sensing and broadband photodetection
Abstract: The light detection in the broadband ranging from ultraviolet to near infrared regime has engrossed substantial attention owing to several applications such as environmental monitoring, optical communication, spectral switching, infrared imaging and memory storage. In this work, we have used WO3 metal oxide semiconductor in the nano particle (NP) state with a wide bandgap as well as higher optical absorption coefficient presenting pronounced potential in the broadband (300–1100 nm) photodetection field. The prepared cost-effective Ag/WO3NPs/p-Si heterojunction photodetector (PD) devices were successfully interpreted by I-V data in dark/illumination, EQE, D*, responsivity and NEP as a function of annealing process. At 3 V bias, the superior photosensing parameters such as responsivity of 3261 A/W, specific detectivity of 3.1×1015- 9.7×1015 Jones and EQE of 2.1×105-4.7×105% were achieved. At 0 V, the 500 ℃ PD device exhibited superior (Formula presented) values of 810 ms/680 ms at 370 nm and 260 ms/380 ms at 1000 nm light illumination. Acetone was used as the target analyte to evaluate the gas sensing capabilities at 200 and 300 °C under variable flow rates (60–300 sccm) using nitrogen as a carrier gas; among the post-annealed samples, the 700 °C device exhibited the highest sensing response (74%) and the fastest dynamics, reaching response/recovery times as low as 15/45 s. Thus, our present work sheds light on the notable potential of Ag/WO3NPs/p-Si heterojunctions in the field of broadband photodetection as well as acetone gas sensing. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Biomimetic coiled PVDF-HFP Fiber-based flexible triboelectric nanogenerator for self-powered interactive electronics
Abstract: Inspired by nature, biomimicry is an efficient approach for producing mechanically robust stretchable coiled nanoarchitectures that can be integrated with lightweight, wearable, energy-harvesting devices. Herein, we report electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) membranes with a bio-inspired coiled fiber architecture, which facilitates the development of crystalline domains enriched in the electroactive β- and γ- phases. This unique morphology imparts enhanced mechanical robustness, an exceptionally high electroactive phase content (91%), and improved contact electrification performance, making the membranes highly promising for energy harvesting and self-powered sensing applications. Remarkably, PVDF-HFP 3 exhibited a tensile strength of 6.17 ± 2.4 MPa, and an elongation at break of 271 ± 22%, which was higher than those of electrospun PVDF (25 ± 04%) and non-coiled PVDF-HFP 2 (195 ± 07%) samples. The triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) device fabricated using PVDF-HFP 3 and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as the triboelectric pair generated an open circuit voltage (VOC) of 1080 VPP, a short-circuit current density (JSC) of ∼15 mAPP m−2, and a peak power density of 1.3 W m−2 at an applied force of 10 N. These values represent a ten-fold enhancement over that of the non-coiled PVDF-HFP-based device. Furthermore, a self-powered wireless electronic drum (E-drum) was developed by integrating a PVDF-HFP/PDMS triboelectric sensor array with a 3D-printed ring-shaped structure and a custom-designed Arduino Uno R4 Wi-Fi platform, enabling the conversion of mechanical tapping inputs into digital signals. The system was integrated with an MP3 player module containing pre-stored drum sounds, allowing real-time audio output upon tapping. This demonstration highlights the practical potential of biomimetic coiled-fiber TENGs and opens new avenues for their application in wearable electronics, intelligent musical interfaces, and advanced human–machine communication systems. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
